summary: Backend-only test of the new object-storage vault + photo-gallery endpoints. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_vault_object_storage.py (16 tests covering /api/vault/upload, /file/{id}, /image/{id}, /photos/{owner_id}). 14/16 pass. Object storage IS the primary path (storage_type=object_storage confirmed), downloads return the original bytes intact, image preview serves inline, and /photos/{owner_id} correctly returns only image documents with proper auth. One real HIGH-priority bug found: thumbnail_url is always None on the upload response and in the persisted document (thumbnail bytes are uploaded to object storage, but the URL is dropped).

critical.issue: thumbnail_url is None for every image upload even though the thumbnail bytes are successfully written to Emergent Object Storage. Response shows storage_type=object_storage + file_url populated (via local fallback) but thumbnail_url=None. Also persisted to MongoDB as None, so the /photos/{owner_id} gallery UI has no thumbnail to render — defeats the primary goal of this iteration.

minor.issue: Returns {redirect_url: null} whenever thumbnail_url is null (same root cause as above). Behaves correctly once the URL bug is fixed, but currently a client that trusts the thumbnail flag gets a redirect_url of null and no image bytes.

Pre-existing 500 in access log: `AttributeError: 'DeleteResult' object has no attribute 'modified_count'` when document is deleted (permanent path returns delete_result but the final `if result.modified_count == 0 and result.deleted_count == 0` check is fine — traceback appears in earlier iterations' cleanup calls). Not introduced by this iteration but still open.

Not exercised in this iteration, but reading the code: it still writes to db.document_files (base64 collection) instead of updating storage_type on the parent document, so subsequent /file/{file_id} downloads for a new-version file_id would miss the object-storage branch and fall through to the base64 fallback (which will 404 because content field isn't stored). Worth fixing next.

action_items: Fix thumbnail_url fallback in /app/backend/routes/document_vault_routes.py near line 123: replace `thumbnail_url = thumb_result.get('url')` with `thumbnail_url = thumb_result.get('url') or f"/api/vault/image/{file_id}?thumbnail=true"` (or add a dedicated `/api/vault/thumbnail/{file_id}` route that serves from storage_service.get_object(thumb_path)). Persist the resulting URL on the document so /photos/{owner_id} can render gallery tiles.

Once thumbnail_url has a real URL, also verify that GET /api/vault/image/{file_id}?thumbnail=true streams the thumbnail bytes rather than returning a JSON payload with redirect_url — the current JSON-return-for-thumbnail-else-Response mismatch will surprise frontend consumers.
Consider updating /api/vault/document/{document_id}/new-version to use storage_service and set storage_type=object_storage on the parent doc so downloads keep working after version bumps.
critical_code_review_comments: document_vault_routes.upload_document: thumbnail_url has no local fallback, unlike file_url on line 103. Emergent Object Storage's put_object() response does not carry a 'url' key in the current environment, so this line always resolves to None. Confirmed via 14 green tests + 2 failures pointing exactly at this line.

storage_service._put returns raw resp.json() from Emergent Object Storage — its schema is not stable/documented at the caller site. Consider always returning `{'path': path, 'url': resp.json().get('url')}` so callers stop needing to double-guard.

get_image_preview mixes two response shapes: JSON `{redirect_url: ...}` when thumbnail=true, else `Response(bytes)`. Downstream JS has to branch on Content-Type. Prefer always streaming the thumbnail bytes when thumbnail=true (via storage_service.get_object on the thumb storage_path) so the endpoint has a single contract.

delete_document permanent path prints 500s in backend.err.log (`DeleteResult has no modified_count`) — carry-over from an earlier iteration, not caused by this change; still worth addressing since test cleanup regularly triggers it.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Object storage plumbing works end-to-end for the primary file (upload → put_object → storage_type=object_storage; GET /vault/file/{id} pulls it back with matching bytes; GET /vault/image/{id} inlines). /vault/photos/{owner_id} correctly filters to file_type ^image/ and honors owner/admin auth + pagination. The one remaining defect is a missing URL fallback for thumbnail_url — fixing that single line should turn the last 2 failures green without any other regression. Do NOT change the tests to accept thumbnail_url=None; the whole point of the iteration is to render actual thumbnails in the fleet gallery.
rca_of_the_issue: Emergent Object Storage's PUT /objects/{path} response (see services/storage_service.py::_put) returns JSON that does not contain a 'url' key in this environment. document_vault_routes.upload_document handles this correctly for file_url (line 103: `storage_result.get('url', f"/api/vault/file/{file_id}")`), but NOT for the thumbnail (line 123: `thumbnail_url = thumb_result.get('url')` with no default), so thumbnail_url is always None even when the thumbnail bytes were successfully written to object storage. Repro: POST /api/vault/upload with any image/png; response.document.thumbnail_url is null and the persisted document (GET /api/vault/document/{document_id}) also shows thumbnail_url=null. Fix: give thumbnail_url the same fallback pattern (e.g., `/api/vault/image/{file_id}?thumbnail=true`) and ensure GET /api/vault/image/{file_id}?thumbnail=true actually streams thumb bytes from storage_service.get_object(thumb_storage_path).
